title: Mixed partials and equality of differentiation orders
terms: higher-order partial derivative; mixed partial derivative; Clairaut theorem; Schwarz theorem.

For which real k can a C function on R satisfy f = 2xy + 3y and f = x + kxy + sin y?
x y
(A) 0 (B) 2 (C) 3 (D) 6 (E) No real k

solution.text:
Equality of mixed partials requires 2x + 6y = 2x + ky for all (x, y), so k = 6. This condition
2 2
is also achievable: f = x y + 3xy − cos y has exactly these two first partial derivatives when
k = 6.

The first summand is quadratic in x, so three x-derivatives annihilate it. The second is
quadratic in y, so four y-derivatives annihilate it. All derivatives are continuous on the
domain, allowing the convenient order for each summand; no expansion of the other factor
is needed.
